Application Materials.content:
- Submit all supporting documents with your application; upload **each supporting document separately** (do not combine files into one document) and give each file a relevant title that clearly states what it contains. If you have already submitted an application, email outstanding documents to [pgadmissions.ambs@manchester.ac.uk](mailto:pgadmissions.ambs@manchester.ac.uk) and include your ID number.
- **Statement of purpose:** tell why you are interested in the course, how it will impact your future, and what makes you stand out as an exceptional candidate. Your statement should be **no more than one page**.
- **Academic transcript and degree certificate:** submit a copy of your official transcript, including modules and grades obtained to date. If you have already graduated, submit your degree certificate and final degree transcript confirming the title of your award, final grade and date of completion. If these documents are not in English, attach an official certified translation. Original copies are not required during the application process.
- **Academic references:** you are **not required to submit an academic reference** when you complete your online application, but after an initial assessment you may be contacted and asked to provide one.
- **CV:** if you have **more than two years' postgraduate work experience** you need to submit your CV.
- **University grading scale:** if you are studying outside the UK, you need to provide the grading scale from your university.
- **Proof of English language ability:** if English is not your first language, you must submit evidence of your English language ability before a decision will be made on your application. If you have studied in a majority English-speaking country, upload a copy of either your visa, CAS, BRP card, or an official letter from your undergraduate institution confirming where your studies were conducted; this can be uploaded within the same file as your CV. Find out more about [language requirements >>](https://www.alliancembs.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/masters-entry-requirements/).
- **Copy of passport:** if you are an international student who needs a Tier 4 visa to study in the UK, you will need to submit a copy of your passport with your application.

Academic Requirements.content:
- We require a **First or Upper Second class honours degree (2:1, with 60% average)** from a UK university or the overseas equivalent.
- Your degree background must be in a **quantitative subject** such as mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, computing, management science or economics, and we require you to demonstrate study of **quantitative modules** (e.g. maths, statistics, calculus) consistently throughout each year of your studies and achieve good grades.
- Study of programming is desirable, but **mathematical-related modules are essential**.
- When assessing your academic record we take into account your grade average, position in class and the standing of the institution where you studied your qualification. We particularly welcome applicants from institutions of high ranking and repute.
- For applicants from **China (Mainland)**: taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a **minimum overall average grade of 80%** or a **minimum GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)** will be considered for admission on to taught master's programmes; please refer to the entrance requirements of individual programmes for further guidance.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: For the one-year pre-experience business master's courses, the most important element of your application is your current GPA. **GMAT and/or GRE are not required for entry.** Unlike the USA there is no history of testing for these courses in England; academic skills evidenced by your GPA are what we will look at.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- For Alliance MBS master's courses, the most recent English language test submitted with the application is the only one accepted. English test scores must be **no more than two years old at the start of the course**.
- Accepted tests and minimum scores:
- [IELTS](http://www.ielts.org/): **7.0 overall and no other element below 6.5**.
- [TOEFL](http://www.ets.org/toefl): **100 overall with a minimum score of 22 in other elements**.
- [Cambridge Proficiency Examination (CPE)](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/): **minimum grade B**.
- [Cambridge Advanced Examination (CAE)](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/): **minimum grade B**.
- English for Academic Purposes (EAP): **overall grade A with minimum grade B in all components**.
- Indian Standard XII English (CBSE and ISC): **minimum 85%**.
- [PTE Academic](https://pearsonpte.com/): **overall score of 76, with a minimum 70 in other elements**.
- For a pre-sessional English language course, the minimum is **IELTS 6.5 overall with no element below 6.0**. See [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.ucae.manchester.ac.uk/study/).
- The following are **not accepted**: TOEFL Home Edition, IELTS Indicator, Duolingo English Test, GMAT, and GRE. A combination of two test scores or TOEFL "MyBest" Scores is also not accepted; applicants must meet the minimum requirements **in one sitting**.
- If an applicant has completed **between one and two years of study in the UK**, an English language test score must be submitted.
- If an applicant has completed a **minimum of three years of undergraduate study within a majority English-speaking country** and has **graduated within the last two years**, an English language test is not required. Applicants who graduated more than two years ago and have remained in an English-speaking country to work or study may also be exempt, **at the discretion of the Admissions Team**. The list of majority English-speaking countries is [here](http://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/language-requirements/).
- If an applicant has completed **one to two years of study within a majority English-speaking country**, they must submit an English language test score. If they studied in a majority English-speaking country, they should upload a copy of their visa, CAS, BRP card, or an official letter from their undergraduate institution confirming where the studies were conducted.
- If an application is submitted without an English language test score, it can be processed, but **no offer can be made until there is evidence of English language ability**. If a test date is already arranged, it should be noted on the application.
- If the score is slightly below the minimum requirements, the minimum IELTS score to consider the application is **6.5 overall with no element below 6.0**. On receiving an offer, applicants may either re-take IELTS to achieve **7.0 overall with no other element below 6.5** or may be eligible for a pre-sessional English course at The University of Manchester.
- To submit scores, scanned copies of score reports are accepted and verified by the Admissions team. Applicants should include their scores and test date on the application form. Results do not need to be sent electronically through the examination centre because the Admissions team can verify them directly using the IELTS TRF Number, TOEFL Appointment Number, or Pearson Score Report Code. If the application has already been submitted without an English language test, results should be emailed directly to the Admissions team.

Program Overview.content:
Master of Science (**MSc**), **1 year**, **full-time**.
With MSc Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence, you will learn the fundamental theories, approaches and analytical toolkit of data analytics, decision sciences, applied operational research and statistics. You will apply this knowledge to real-life scenarios to enhance your learning.
This MSc prepares you to lead data-driven decision-making in organisations using advanced analytics and AI.
- Tackle real business challenges using applied AI methods and industry-standard analytical tools, building practical capability alongside strong theoretical foundations.
- Develop advanced expertise in machine learning, data analytics and strategic optimisation, equipping you to improve performance and manage risk in complex environments.
- Learn from research-active experts connected to the Centre for AI and Decision Sciences, ensuring your studies reflect current industry and technological developments.
- Apply your skills through substantial project work, strengthening your ability to translate analytical insight into strategic action.
- Benefit from the programme’s relaunch for September 2026 with an enhanced focus on AI for Business, and tailor your studies through optional units aligned to your career ambitions.
**Formerly MSc Business Analytics, Operational Research and Risk Analysis, this course has been reviewed and relaunched from September 2026, with an increased emphasis on AI for Business.**

Financial Aid.content:
- **Global Futures Scholarship**: **£18,000 for Africa, £10,000 for other select markets**. Offered to international students starting their studies in **September 2026** at The University of Manchester; applicants must hold an offer for a course starting in September 2026, and an online application form will be emailed to relevant offer-holders. [Learn more about the Global Futures Scholarship](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/finance-and-scholarships/funding/global-futures-scholarship/)
- **Manchester Alumni Loyalty Discount**: **10% discount on tuition fees**. Offered to alumni of The University of Manchester enrolling on one of the Business School's taught master's courses. [Learn more about the Manchester Alumni Loyalty Discount](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/fees-and-funding/masters-student-funding/manchester-alumni-loyalty-discount/)
- **Manchester Master's Bursary**: **£4,000 bursary**. Supports students from underrepresented backgrounds in the **UK** to access postgraduate study at The University of Manchester. [Learn more about the Manchester Master’s Bursary](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/fees-and-funding/masters-student-funding/masters-bursary/)
- **Sports Scholarships**: Value varies by recipient. Supports students from all countries balancing study with achieving their aspirations to continue moving up their sporting pathway. [Learn more about Sport Scholarships](https://www.sport.manchester.ac.uk/sport-and-activity/scholarships/)
- **Talented Athlete Scholarship Scheme (TASS)**: Value varies by recipient. Supports talented athletes in education with performance sport experts and experienced practitioners. [Learn more about the TASS](https://www.sport.manchester.ac.uk/sport-and-activity/scholarships/tass/)
- **British Chevening Scholarship**: **Fully funded scholarship** for high calibre international students with leadership potential. [Learn more about Chevening Scholarships](https://www.chevening.org/scholarships/)
- **Indonesia Endowment Fund for Education (LPDP)**: Value varies by scholarship type; provides scholarships for Indonesian citizens pursuing higher education domestically and internationally. [Learn more about the LPDP](https://lpdp.kemenkeu.go.id/en/)
- **Commonwealth Scholarships and Fellowships Plan (CSFP) General Scholarship**: Award: Studentship; value varies by recipient. Open to Commonwealth citizens, refugees or British protected persons permanently resident in any Commonwealth country other than the UK. [Learn more about the CSFP](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/fees-and-funding/masters-student-funding/database/display/?id=00000019&offset=0&sort=name&sortdir=ascending&subjectArea=Business%20and%20Management&nationality=Australia&submit=Search)
- **Fulbright Scholarships**: Value varies by recipient; for applicants from the **USA only** and includes tuition and living expenses. [Learn more about Fulbright Scholarships](https://us.fulbrightonline.org/applicants/getting-started)
- **Canada Centennial Scholarship Fund (CCSF)**: **£5,000 annually** for eligible Canadians studying for a postgraduate degree who have completed their first year of study. [Learn more about the CCSF](https://www.canadianscholarshipfund.co.uk/)
- Government of Canada scholarships are also available. [Learn more about Government of Canada scholarships](https://www.educanada.ca/scholarships-bourses/index.aspx?lang=eng)
- **US Marshall Scholarship**: Value varies by recipient for United States citizens who, when they take up the scholarship, hold a first degree from an accredited four-year college or university in the United States. [Learn more about the US Marshall Scholarship](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/)
- **Postgraduate Solutions Study Bursaries**: **£2,000 bursary**. Every postgraduate student is eligible to apply, regardless of subject choice or study mode, and the bursary can top up other funding already secured. [Learn more about Postgraduate Solutions Study Bursaries](https://www.postgrad.com/psuk_study_bursaries_apply/)

Multiple Applications.content: Yes, you can apply for more than one course. If an application fee is required, you need to pay for **each course** you wish to apply for. MSc Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence requires a **non-refundable application fee of £60**. [Check the application fee for Master's courses](https://www.alliancembs.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/how-to-apply/)

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- To defer your offer to the following year, you must contact your admission officer to get a copy of the deferral form.
- You can only defer your place for **one year**.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- AMBS is unable to make aspirational offers. If you submit your application before you've completed your undergraduate degree, your current average grade must meet our minimum entry requirements for your application to be considered.
- If your score is slightly below the minimum English requirements, then on receiving an offer for an AMBS master's course, you will be given the option to re-take IELTS to achieve **7.0 overall with no other element below 6.5** or you may be eligible to attend a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.ucae.manchester.ac.uk/study/). This formal recommendation is an alternative option to retaking an English Language test and only comes as a condition in your official offer letter.
- If your English language ability is slightly below our requirements, you may be eligible for a pre-sessional English language course in order to progress to the Masters degree. You must achieve a minimum IELTS score of **6.5 overall with no element below 6.0** for entry to a pre-sessional course.
- If you have already met our academic requirements and English language requirements, a single visa may be issued covering both the pre-sessional course and the Masters degree. If, however, you obtain a conditional offer for the Master degree and your academic results are pending you may still enrol in a pre-sessional course on a separate visa.
- If you haven’t completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a Pre-sessional English course prior to a Masters degree, AMBS strongly recommends that you take the UKVI IELTS test to ensure you are eligible for a separate visa for the language course.
